quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest to do?

options.text: Change your speed often to stay alert.
Drive at the same speed as other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other cars. Always drive at the same speed as traffic around you, but never faster than the speed limit.

questions.question: What can happen if you lie on a DMV application?

options.text: Your license can be suspended for one year.

questions.explanation: Lying on a DMV application can result in a one-year license suspension. It is also a serious crime that can lead to fines and jail time.

questions.question: What does a red traffic light mean?
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. Stop at the stop line and before any crosswalk.

questions.question: What sign is this?
questions.explanation: This is a yield sign. When you see this sign, slow down and check for traffic. Let pedestrians and other cars go first. Stop only if you need to.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station nearby.
Slow down and let trains pass first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass first.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you of a railroad crossing ahead. Slow down when you approach the tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass.

questions.question: What should you do if your gas pedal gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and push hard on the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and push hard on the brake.
questions.explanation: If your gas pedal sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral right away and press the brake firmly. When it is safe, pull to the side and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: Is driving at night safer or more dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: When should seat belts be worn?

options.text: By all people in the car every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: By all people in the car every time.
questions.explanation: Everyone in the car must wear a seat belt every time you drive. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object in a crash and hurt others.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from it if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass it quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from it if possible.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space if you can safely do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down below the speed limit and give it as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, let other traffic go first, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must let you in.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, let other traffic go first, and merge at the same speed as traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging, signal and enter at the same speed as other traffic. Always let other traffic go first when entering a roadway.

questions.question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your car slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tires increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also increases the risk.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming cars.
Your car can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can clearly see the road ahead, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your car is capable of the speed needed to pass. Do not pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: The most common color of warning signs is:
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Just as safe as normal driving.

questions.explanation: Distracted driving is extremely risky. It endangers you, your passengers, pedestrians, bicyclists, and other drivers. Staying focused on the road prevents crashes.

questions.question: Who is most likely to be killed in a work zone crash?
questions.explanation: Drivers and passengers are more likely to be killed in a work zone crash than others. Drive carefully in roadwork areas.

questions.question: Driving at night requires increased caution because:

options.text: There are more cars on the road at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: It is dark at night, so drivers cannot see as well. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or when people and vehicles are not visible for 500 feet.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and react to surprises.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers turning left on a green light to let oncoming traffic go first. You can complete your turn when it is safe.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger instead of the road while talking.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking mirrors, and watching your dashboard. These safe habits keep you focused.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights when you cannot see 500 feet ahead. Always use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect off fog and rain, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You see a railroad crossing sign but no gates or flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Approach slowly and only cross when you are sure no train is coming.
Turn down your radio to listen for a train.
Only continue if a flagger tells you it is safe.

questions.explanation: Always approach railroad crossings with caution. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming from either direction. If a flagger is present, follow their instructions.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or in a curve because few cars are coming.
By driving on the shoulder of the road.
When there is a solid yellow line on your side and the other lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Never pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Never pass by driving on the shoulder. Never pass when there is a solid yellow line on your side.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?
questions.explanation: High speeds increase both stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder the impact if you crash.

questions.question: What does a "No stopping" sign mean?

options.text: You may stop only long enough to unload packages.
You may stop only to avoid hitting other vehicles.
You may stop only to let passengers out.
You may stop for less than five minutes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may stop only to avoid hitting other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A "No stopping" sign means you can only stop to follow a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: What can impair your ability to drive?
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires being in good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness can all impair your driving ability.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line with the broken line next to you, can you pass?
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 miles per hour.

questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or ice. Safe driving may require going slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: What happens when drivers eat or drink while driving?

options.text: They are better drivers because they are not hungry.
They have trouble controlling their vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They have trouble controlling their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous. These actions take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road, making it hard to control your vehicle.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up immediately.
Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
Drive faster to get through the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions are not ideal for driving.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn you that work is happening on or near the road. Drive with extra care in these areas.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them more space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass. They can finish passing more quickly and easily.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed if you are at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, no matter which direction you are driving.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
Drive only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance behind other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance lets you react to problems without emergency stops. This prevents drivers behind you from crashing into your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights at an intersection are not working?

options.text: Park off the road and wait for the power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it as a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it as a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When traffic lights are not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop. Then go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: What must you do when a transit bus signals to re-enter the main road after stopping?

options.text: Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to any transit bus that is signaling to return to the main road after picking up or dropping off passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely merge into traffic.
